questions.text: रजत तथा समर एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5: 3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। तरुण को फर्म के लाभों में 2/5 भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया। तरुण अपने भाग की पूँजी के रूप में ₹ 5,00,000 तथा ख्याति प्रीमियम के अपने भाग के रूप में ₹ 3,00,000 लाया। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्य था :
questions.text_english: Rajat and Samar were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5: 3. Tarun was admitted as a new partner for 2/5th share in the profits of the firm. Tarun brought ₹ 5,00,000 as his share of capital and ₹ 3,00,000 as his share of goodwill premium. The value of goodwill of the firm was:
questions.solution: The value of the firm's goodwill is determined by the new partner's share and the premium brought in by him. Tarun brings ₹ 3,00,000 as goodwill premium for a 2/5th share in the profits. Therefore, the total goodwill of the firm is calculated by multiplying his premium by the reciprocal of his share, which is ₹ 3,00,000 * (5/2), equating to ₹ 7,50,000. Hence, the correct option is A.

questions.text_english: Elvis, Finch and Gordon entered into a partnership on 1st July, 2023 with capitals of ₹ 20,00,000 each. The partnership deed provided for interest on capital @ 10% per annum. The firm earned a net profit of ₹ 13,50,000 for the year ended 31st March, 2024. The amount of profit transferred to Elvis's capital account was:
questions.solution: First, the interest on capital for each partner must be calculated for nine months from 1st July, 2023 to 31st March, 2024. For each partner, it is ₹ 20,00,000 at 10% for 9/12 months, which equals ₹ 1,50,000. Total interest on capital for all three partners is ₹ 4,50,000. Subtracting this from the net profit of ₹ 13,50,000 leaves a divisible profit of ₹ 9,00,000. Since no profit-sharing ratio is mentioned, the profit is distributed equally. Thus, Elvis's share of the profit is one-third of ₹ 9,00,000, which is ₹ 3,00,000. The correct option is B.

questions.text_english: Diksha Ltd. invited applications for issuing 1,00,000 equity shares of ₹ 10 each at a premium of 10%. The whole amount was payable on application. Applications were received for 3,00,000 equity shares. The company decided to allot the shares on pro-rata basis to all the applicants. The amount refunded by the company was:
questions.solution: The issue price of the shares is ₹ 11 each (₹ 10 face value plus a 10% premium). Because the entire issue price is payable entirely upon application, there are no subsequent calls (like allotment or first call) to adjust any excess application money against. Therefore, even though the company stated it was on a pro-rata basis, the excess application money for the 2,00,000 shares cannot be held and must be entirely refunded. The amount refunded is 2,00,000 shares multiplied by the application price of ₹ 11, which equals ₹ 22,00,000. Thus, option A is correct.

questions.text:
'एक साझेदारी फर्म का व्यवसाय सभी साझेदारों द्वारा अथवा सभी साझेदारों की तरफ से किसी एक साझेदार द्वारा किया जा सकता है।'
उपर्युक्त कथन निम्नलिखित में से साझेदारी की किस विशेषता पर प्रकाश डालता है ?
questions.text_english:
'The business of a partnership firm may be carried on by all the partners or any of them acting for all.'
The above statement highlights which of the following feature of partnership?
questions.solution: The statement 'business carried on by all or any of them acting for all' defines the relationship of mutual agency in a partnership, where each partner can act as both an agent binding the other partners through their actions and as a principal being bound by the actions of the others. Thus, option D is the correct answer.

questions.text: रीमा, मीशा तथा शिखा एक साझेदारी फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 8 : 7 : 5 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं । 1 अक्टूबर, 2023 को रीमा ने फर्म को ₹ 5,00,000 का एक ऋण दिया। यहाँ कोई साझेदारी संलेख नहीं है। रीमा के ऋण पर ब्याज लगाने से पूर्व 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ ₹ 2,15,000 था। शिखा के पूँजी खाते में क्रेडिट की गई लाभ की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Reema, Meesha and Shikha were partners in a partnership firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 8:7:5. On 1st October, 2023, Reema advanced a loan of ₹ 5,00,000 to the firm. There is no partnership deed. The firm's profit for the year ended 31st March, 2024 before charging interest on Reema's loan amounted to ₹ 2,15,000. The amount of profit credited to Shikha's capital account was:
questions.solution: In the absence of a partnership deed, interest on a partner's loan is provided at 6% p.a. The interest on Reema's loan for the six months from 1st October, 2023 to 31st March, 2024 is ₹ 5,00,000 * 6% * 6/12 = ₹ 15,000. This interest is a charge against profit, so the divisible net profit becomes ₹ 2,15,000 - ₹ 15,000 = ₹ 2,00,000. This profit is distributed in the ratio of 8:7:5. Shikha's share is 5/20 of the divisible profit. Thus, Shikha's share = ₹ 2,00,000 * (5/20) = ₹ 50,000. The correct option is C.

questions.text: व्हाइट, शॉन तथा टॉड एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा लाभ-हानि का विभाजन बराबर-बराबर करते थे। शॉन की पत्नी ने फर्म को ₹ 1,00,000 का ऋण पहले से दिया हुआ था। फर्म का विघटन हो गया। शॉन की पत्नी का ऋण पहले ही वसूली खाते में हस्तांतरित कर दिया गया था। शॉन की पत्नी के ऋण का भुगतान करने पर क्रेडिट किया जाने वाला खाता था :
questions.text_english: White, Shaun and Todd were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Shaun's wife had advanced a loan of ₹ 1,00,000 to the firm. The firm was dissolved. Shaun's wife's loan had already been transferred to Realisation account. The account credited to discharge Shaun's wife's loan will be:
questions.solution: When an external liability, such as a partner's relative's loan, is already transferred to the Realisation Account upon the dissolution of a firm, the payment to discharge this liability results in an outflow of cash or bank funds. Consequently, the Realisation Account is debited, and the Bank Account (or Cash Account) is credited. Therefore, the Bank Account is the account to be credited, making option B the correct answer.

questions.text: नीरू तथा पूजा एक साझेदारी फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 4: 3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं। पिछले कुछ वर्षों में फर्म ने ₹ 5,00,000 का औसत लाभ अर्जित किया। समान व्यवसाय में सामान्य प्रतिफल दर 10% है। फर्म का औसत अधिलाभ ₹ 4,00,000 था। फर्म द्वारा विनियोजित पूँजी की राशि थी :
questions.text_english: Neeru and Pooja were partners in a partnership firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4: 3. The firm earned average profits of ₹ 5,00,000 during the last few years. The normal rate of return in a similar business is 10%. The average super profits of the firm were ₹ 4,00,000. The amount of capital employed by the firm was:
questions.solution: Super profit is determined by subtracting normal profit from the average profit. With an average profit of ₹ 5,00,000 and a super profit of ₹ 4,00,000, the normal profit must be ₹ 1,00,000. Normal profit is calculated as the capital employed multiplied by the normal rate of return. Given a 10% rate of return, capital employed * 10% = ₹ 1,00,000. By solving this equation, the capital employed is found to be ₹ 10,00,000. Hence, option D is correct.

questions.text:
अभिकथन (A) : साझेदारों के वेतन को लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाते में डेबिट किया जाता है न कि लाभ-हानि खाते में।
कारण (R) : साझेदारों का वेतन लाभ का विनियोग है, यह लाभों के विरुद्ध एक प्रभार नहीं है।
निम्नलिखित में से सही विकल्प का चयन कीजिए :
questions.text_english:
Assertion (A): Partners' salary is debited to Profit and Loss Appropriation Account and not to Profit and Loss Account.
Reason (R): Partners' salary is an appropriation of profit, it is not a charge against profits.
Choose the correct option from the following:

options.A: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं तथा कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या है।
options.B: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों सही हैं, परंतु कारण (R), अभिकथन (A) की सही व्याख्या नहीं है।
options.C: अभिकथन (A) सही है, परंतु कारण (R) ग़लत है।
options.D: अभिकथन (A) तथा कारण (R) दोनों ग़लत हैं।

options_english.A: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.B: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are correct, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
options_english.C: Assertion (A) is correct, but Reason (R) is incorrect.
options_english.D: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are incorrect.

questions.solution: The Assertion correctly states that partners' salaries are debited to the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account and not the standard Profit and Loss Account. The Reason provides the correct justification for this accounting treatment because partners' salaries are indeed an appropriation (distribution) of the net profits earned by the firm rather than a strict business expense (charge against profits). Therefore, both are correct, and the Reason explains the Assertion properly.

questions.text: कबीर तथा लारा एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5: 3 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । मार्क को फर्म के लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया। सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात् मार्क को कबीर तथा लारा की संयुक्त पूँजी के 2/5 भाग के बराबर पूँजी लानी थी। सभी समायोजनों के पश्चात् कबीर तथा लारा की पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 8,00,000 तथा ₹ 7,00,000 थी। मार्क द्वारा लाई गई पूँजी थी :
questions.text_english: Kabir and Lara were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5: 3. Mark was admitted as a new partner for 1/5 share in the profits of the firm. Mark was to bring 2/5th of the combined capital of Kabir and Lara after all adjustments are carried out. The capitals of Kabir and Lara after all adjustments were ₹ 8,00,000 and ₹ 7,00,000 respectively. The capital brought by Mark was:
questions.solution: The combined capital of Kabir and Lara after all adjustments is ₹ 8,00,000 + ₹ 7,00,000 = ₹ 15,00,000. Mark is required to bring capital equal to 2/5th of this combined capital. Thus, the capital to be brought in by Mark is 2/5 * ₹ 15,00,000, which equals ₹ 6,00,000. Therefore, the correct answer is C.

questions.text: प्रखर तथा राजन एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3: 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे, उनकी पूँजी क्रमशः ₹ 10,00,000 तथा ₹ 9,00,000 थी। सिद्धार्थ को फर्म के लाभों में 1/5 भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया। प्रखर, राजन तथा सिद्धार्थ के मध्य 12: 8: 5 के नए लाभ विभाजन अनुपात की सहमति हुई। प्रखर तथा राजन का त्याग अनुपात होगा :
questions.text_english: Prakhar and Rajan were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2 with capitals of ₹ 10,00,000 and ₹ 9,00,000 respectively. Siddharth was admitted as a new partner for 1/5 share in the profits of the firm. The new profit sharing ratio between Prakhar, Rajan and Siddharth was agreed at 12:8:5. The sacrificing ratio of Prakhar and Rajan will be :
questions.solution: The sacrificing ratio is computed by subtracting the new profit share from the old profit share for each partner. Prakhar's old share was 3/5 (or 15/25) and his new share is 12/25. His sacrifice is 15/25 - 12/25 = 3/25. Rajan's old share was 2/5 (or 10/25) and his new share is 8/25. His sacrifice is 10/25 - 8/25 = 2/25. Thus, the sacrificing ratio between Prakhar and Rajan is 3:2, making option A the correct answer.

sub_questions.text: तविश, उमेश तथा वरुन एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 4:3: 2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । तविश सेवानिवृत्त हो गया। उमेश तथा वरुन ने भविष्य में लाभ-हानि 5 : 3 के अनुपात में विभाजित करने का निर्णय लिया। उमेश का अभिलाभ भाग होगा :
sub_questions.text_english: Tavish, Umesh and Varun were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 4:3:2. Tavish retired. Umesh and Varun decided to share profits and losses in future in the ratio of 5: 3. The gaining share of Umesh will be :
sub_questions.solution: To find a partner's gaining share, we subtract their old profit share from their new profit share. Umesh's old share was 3/9. His new share after Tavish's retirement is 5/8. His gaining share is calculated as 5/8 - 3/9. By finding a common denominator of 72, this translates to 45/72 - 24/72, which yields a gaining share of 21/72. Thus, the correct option is A.

sub_questions.text: असित, सोनू तथा हिना एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे । असित सेवानिवृत्त हो गया तथा संचयों व परिसंपत्तियों एवं देयताओं के पुनर्मूल्यांकन के लिए आवश्यक समायोजनों के पश्चात् उसके पूँजी खाते में ₹ 40,00,000 का शेष था। सोनू तथा हिना उसके दावे के पूर्ण निपटान के लिए ₹ 45,00,000 का भुगतान करने के लिए सहमत हो गए। फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्य था :
sub_questions.text_english: Asit, Sonu and Hina were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. Asit retired and the balance in his capital account after making necessary adjustments on account of reserves and revaluation of assets and liabilities was ₹ 40,00,000. Sonu and Hina agreed to pay him ₹ 45,00,000 in full settlement of his claim. The value of goodwill of the firm was:
sub_questions.solution: The extra payment made to the retiring partner over and above their adjusted capital balance represents their share in the firm's hidden goodwill. Asit is paid ₹ 45,00,000 against an adjusted capital of ₹ 40,00,000, signifying his share of the goodwill is ₹ 5,00,000. Since his old profit share was 3/6 (or 1/2), the total goodwill of the firm is computed by dividing his share of goodwill by his profit ratio, i.e., ₹ 5,00,000 / (1/2), equating to ₹ 10,00,000. Thus, option D is correct.

sub_questions.text: अजित, बिस्वास तथा चित्रा एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 5:3:2 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। 30 सितंबर, 2024 को बिस्वास की मृत्यु हो गई। फर्म अपनी पुस्तकें प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को बंद करती है। पिछले स्थिति विवरण की तिथि से उसकी मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ में बिस्वास के भाग की गणना विक्रय के आधार पर की जाएगी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए विक्रय की राशि ₹ 24,00,000 थी तथा 1 अप्रैल, 2024 से 30 सितंबर, 2024 तक यह राशि ₹ 15,00,000 थी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए लाभ ₹ 2,40,000 था। मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभों में बिस्वास का भाग था :
sub_questions.text_english: Ajit, Biswas and Chitra were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5:3:2. Biswas died on 30th September, 2024. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. Biswas's share of profits till the date of death from the last Balance Sheet date, was to be calculated on the basis of sales. Sales for the year ended 31st March, 2024 amounted to ₹ 24,00,000 and that from 1st April, 2024 to 30th September, 2024 amounted to ₹ 15,00,000. The profits for the year ended 31st March, 2024 were ₹ 2,40,000. Biswas's share of profits till the date of his death was:
sub_questions.solution: First, the net profit ratio for the previous year needs to be calculated. The profit was ₹ 2,40,000 on sales of ₹ 24,00,000, yielding a profit percentage of 10% (2.4L / 24L). Applying this 10% rate to the current year's sales up to the date of death (₹ 15,00,000), the estimated profit for this period is ₹ 1,50,000. Biswas's share of this profit is determined by his profit-sharing ratio (3/10). Thus, his share is ₹ 1,50,000 multiplied by 3/10, which equals ₹ 45,000. Therefore, the correct option is C.

sub_questions.text: ईशा, जूली तथा कविता एक फर्म में साझेदार थीं तथा 3:2:1 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करती थीं। फर्म अपनी पुस्तकें प्रति वर्ष 31 मार्च को बंद करती है। 12 जून, 2024 को कविता की मृत्यु हो गई। पिछले स्थिति विवरण की तिथि से उसकी मृत्यु की तिथि तक फर्म के लाभों में उसके भाग की गणना पिछले वर्ष के लाभ के आधार पर की जाएगी । पिछले वर्ष का लाभ ₹ 6,00,000 था। मृत्यु की तिथि तक लाभ में कविता का भाग था :
sub_questions.text_english: Isha, Julie and Kavita were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3:2:1. The firm closes its books on 31st March every year. On 12th June, 2024, Kavita died. Her share in the profits of the firm from the last Balance Sheet till the date of death was to be calculated on the basis of last year's profit. Last year's profits were ₹ 6,00,000. Kavita's share of profit till the date of her death was:
sub_questions.solution: The number of days from the start of the financial year (1st April, 2024) to Kavita's death (12th June, 2024) is 73 days (30 days in April + 31 days in May + 12 days in June). This represents exactly 1/5th of a year (73/365). The estimated profit for the whole year is taken as ₹ 6,00,000. The estimated profit for the 73 days is ₹ 6,00,000 * 1/5 = ₹ 1,20,000. Kavita's share of this profit is determined by her ratio of 1/6. Therefore, her share is ₹ 1,20,000 * 1/6, which equals ₹ 20,000. Option A is correct.

sub_questions.solution: The loss on the issue of debentures represents the future liability that a company incurs when it commits to redeeming the debentures at a premium. Although issued at a premium (which is a capital profit), the premium payable on redemption is treated as a loss on issue. Here, the premium on redemption is 10% of the face value (₹ 100), which is ₹ 10 per debenture. For 20,000 debentures, the total loss on issue is 20,000 multiplied by ₹ 10, which equates to ₹ 2,00,000. Therefore, option A is correct.

Discount on issue of debentures, ₹ 1,00,000 was completely written off through Statement of Profit and Loss on 31st March, 2024. On issue of debentures, 'Debentures Account' was credited with

questions.text:
निशु, ऋशु तथा किशु एक फर्म में साझेदार थे तथा 8: 7: 5 के अनुपात में लाभ-हानि का विभाजन करते थे। 1 अप्रैल, 2024 से उन्होंने भविष्य के लाभ-हानि 5: 8: 7 के अनुपात में विभाजित करने का निर्णय किया। 31 मार्च, 2024 को उनका स्थिति विवरण निम्नलिखित दर्शा रहा था :
(i) सामान्य संचय ₹ 10,00,000
(ii) लाभ-हानि खाते में ₹ 2,00,000 का डेबिट शेष।
फर्म की ख्याति का मूल्यांकन ₹ 20,00,000 किया गया तथा परिसंपत्तियों तथा देयताओं के पुनर्मूल्यांकन के परिणामस्वरूप ₹ 7,00,000 का लाभ हुआ। साझेदार सामान्य संचय तथा लाभ-हानि खाते के शेष को बाँटना नहीं चाहते थे। उन्होंने यह भी निर्णय लिया कि परिसंपत्तियों तथा देयताओं के पुनर्मूल्यांकित मूल्यों का लेखा पुस्तकों में नहीं किया जाएगा। उपर्युक्त को प्रभावी बनाने के लिए एक एकल समायोजन प्रविष्टि कीजिए। अपने कार्य को स्पष्ट रूप से दर्शाइए ।
questions.text_english:
Nishu, Rishu and Kishu were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 8:7: 5. They decided to share future profits and losses in the ratio of 5:8: 7 with effect from 1st April, 2024. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024 showed :
(i) General Reserve ₹ 10,00,000.
(ii) Debit Balance of ₹ 2,00,000 in Profit and Loss Account.
Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 20,00,000 and revaluation of assets and liabilities resulted in a profit of ₹ 7,00,000. The partners did not want to distribute the General Reserve and the balance of Profit and Loss Account. They also decided that revalued values of assets and liabilities were not to be recorded in the books.
Pass a single adjustment entry to give effect to the above. Show your workings clearly.

key_points: Calculate net effect of all items: Gen. Reserve (10,00,000) - P&L Dr Bal (2,00,000) + Goodwill (20,00,000) + Revaluation Profit (7,00,000) = ₹ 35,00,000 (Positive/Credit balance).
Calculate sacrifice/gain: Nishu = 8/20 - 5/20 = +3/20 (Sacrifice); Rishu = 7/20 - 8/20 = -1/20 (Gain); Kishu = 5/20 - 7/20 = -2/20 (Gain).
Journal Entry: Rishu's Capital A/c Dr. 1,75,000; Kishu's Capital A/c Dr. 3,50,000; To Nishu's Capital A/c 5,25,000.

questions.solution:
When partners decide to alter their profit-sharing ratio without distributing reserves, accumulated profits, losses, or incorporating revalued figures, a single adjustment entry must be passed through their capital accounts based on the net effect. First, the net effect is calculated. This is the sum of General Reserve (₹ 10,00,000), Goodwill (₹ 20,00,000), and Revaluation Profit (₹ 7,00,000), minus the Profit and Loss debit balance (₹ 2,00,000), which results in a net positive adjustment figure of ₹ 35,00,000.

Next, the sacrifice or gain for each partner is calculated by subtracting the new ratio from the old ratio. The old ratio is 8:7:5 (out of 20) and the new ratio is 5:8:7 (out of 20).
Nishu's share: 8/20 - 5/20 = 3/20 (Sacrifice)
Rishu's share: 7/20 - 8/20 = -1/20 (Gain)
Kishu's share: 5/20 - 7/20 = -2/20 (Gain)

The gaining partners (Rishu and Kishu) compensate the sacrificing partner (Nishu) based on the net adjustment value. 
Rishu's debit amount = ₹ 35,00,000 * 1/20 = ₹ 1,75,000.
Kishu's debit amount = ₹ 35,00,000 * 2/20 = ₹ 3,50,000.
Nishu's credit amount = ₹ 35,00,000 * 3/20 = ₹ 5,25,000.

The final journal entry is:
Rishu's Capital A/c Dr. ₹ 1,75,000 
Kishu's Capital A/c Dr. ₹ 3,50,000
To Nishu's Capital A/c ₹ 5,25,000. 
(Being the net adjustment made for reserves, accumulated losses, goodwill, and revaluation due to the change in profit-sharing ratio).

31 मार्च, 2024 को सुधीर तथा बलवीर का स्थिति विवरण

1 अप्रैल, 2024 को सुशांत को निम्नलिखित शर्तों पर फर्म के लाभों में 1/9 भाग के लिए एक नए साझेदार के रूप में प्रवेश दिया गया :
(i) निवेशों का बाज़ार मूल्य ₹ 60,00,000 था।
(ii) कामगार क्षतिपूर्ति के खाते के दावे का अनुमान ₹ 41,00,000 लगाया गया।

questions.text_english:
Sudhir and Balbir were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5: 4. The following is the extract of their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024.
Balance Sheet of Sudhir and Balbir as at 31st March, 2024
[Table in Image]
On 1st April, 2024, Sushant was admitted as a new partner for 1/9th share in the profits of the firm on the following terms:
(i) Market value of investments was ₹ 60,00,000.
(ii) Claim on account of Workmen Compensation was estimated at ₹ 41,00,000.
Pass necessary journal entries for treatment of Investment Fluctuation Fund and Workmen Compensation Fund on the date of Sushant's admission.

key_points: Record drop in investment value: 75L - 60L = 15L. IFF covers this drop entirely as IFF = 15L.
Entry 1: Investment Fluctuation Fund Dr 15,00,000 To Investments 15,00,000.
Record workmen compensation claim of 41L against WCF of 50L. Remaining 9L goes to partners in 5:4 ratio.
Entry 2: Workmen Compensation Fund Dr 50,00,000 To Provision for Workmen Compensation Claim 41,00,000, To Sudhir's Capital A/c 5,00,000, To Balbir's Capital A/c 4,00,000.

questions.solution:
When a new partner is admitted, specific reserve funds are adjusted to account for market changes and claims before establishing the new capital structure. 

For the Investment Fluctuation Fund (IFF), the investments have dropped in value from ₹ 75,00,000 to ₹ 60,00,000, representing a ₹ 15,00,000 decrease. This deficit is compensated by fully utilizing the IFF of ₹ 15,00,000. The entry is: Debit Investment Fluctuation Fund by ₹ 15,00,000 and Credit Investments by ₹ 15,00,000. 

For the Workmen Compensation Fund (WCF), the fund stands at ₹ 50,00,000, and the actual claim is estimated at ₹ 41,00,000. The excess ₹ 9,00,000 in the fund is distributed among the old partners, Sudhir and Balbir, in their old profit-sharing ratio of 5:4. Thus, Sudhir gets ₹ 5,00,000 and Balbir gets ₹ 4,00,000. The entry is: Debit WCF by ₹ 50,00,000, Credit Provision for Workmen Compensation Claim by ₹ 41,00,000, Credit Sudhir's Capital A/c by ₹ 5,00,000, and Credit Balbir's Capital A/c by ₹ 4,00,000.

questions.text_english: Attempt any one of the following: (a) or (b)

sub_questions.text: 1 अप्रैल, 2024 को अभय तथा सुजोय ने क्रमशः ₹ 80,00,000 तथा ₹ 60,00,000 की पूँजी के साथ एक साझेदारी में प्रवेश किया। साझेदारों ने अपने पूँजी योगदान के अनुपात में लाभ विभाजित करने का निर्णय लिया। उन्होंने वर्ष के दौरान क्रमशः ₹ 6,00,000 तथा ₹ 4,00,000 का आहरण किया। साझेदारी संलेख के प्रावधानों के अनुसार साझेदारों से आहरण पर 10% वार्षिक ब्याज लिया जाता था। सुजोय द्वारा अभय के लाभ के हिस्से की न्यूनतम गारंटी प्रति वर्ष ₹ 3,50,000 दी गई थी। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ ₹ 6,50,000 था। 31 मार्च, 2024 को समाप्त हुए वर्ष के लिए फर्म का लाभ-हानि विनियोजन खाता तैयार कीजिए।
sub_questions.text_english: Abhay and Sujoy entered into partnership on 1st April, 2024 with capitals of ₹ 80,00,000 and ₹ 60,00,000 respectively. The partners decided to share profits in the ratio of their capital contribution. They withdrew ₹ 6,00,000 and ₹ 4,00,000 respectively during the year. The partners were charged interest on drawings @ 10% per annum as per the provisions of the partnership deed. Abhay's share of profit was guaranteed by Sujoy at a minimum of ₹ 3,50,000 per annum. The profit of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2024 amounted to ₹ 6,50,000. Prepare Profit and Loss Appropriation Account of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2024.

key_points: Determine Profit Sharing Ratio based on capital: 80,00,000 : 60,00,000 = 4:3.
Calculate Interest on Drawings: Abhay = 6,00,000 * 10% * 6/12 = 30,000. Sujoy = 4,00,000 * 10% * 6/12 = 20,000. (6 months average period as dates are not given).
Calculate divisible profit: Net Profit (6,50,000) + Interest on Drawings (50,000) = 7,00,000.
Check Guarantee: Abhay's share (4,00,000) exceeds his guaranteed minimum (3,50,000). Thus, no deficiency adjustment is required.
Draft the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account showing Net Profit on the credit side, Interest on Drawings on the credit side, and the final profit distribution on the debit side.

sub_questions.solution:
To prepare the Profit and Loss Appropriation Account, we first establish the profit-sharing ratio. The ratio of their initial capital contributions is ₹ 80,00,000 to ₹ 60,00,000, which simplifies to a 4:3 ratio. 
Next, we calculate the interest on drawings. Because the specific dates of the withdrawals are not provided, we apply the interest rate over an average period of 6 months. For Abhay, it is ₹ 6,00,000 at 10% for half a year, resulting in ₹ 30,000. For Sujoy, it is ₹ 4,00,000 at 10% for half a year, which comes to ₹ 20,000. 
The total divisible profit is the sum of the firm's net profit (₹ 6,50,000) and the total interest on drawings collected (₹ 50,000), making the divisible profit ₹ 7,00,000. 
Allocating this profit in the 4:3 ratio gives Abhay a share of ₹ 4,00,000 (4/7 of 7 Lakhs) and Sujoy a share of ₹ 3,00,000 (3/7 of 7 Lakhs). Since Abhay's computed share of ₹ 4,00,000 is greater than his guaranteed minimum of ₹ 3,50,000, there is no deficiency, and no further adjustment is necessary. 
The Profit and Loss Appropriation Account will reflect the net profit and interest on drawings on the credit side, and the distribution of profits to the partners' capital accounts on the debit side.

Sonia and Shruti were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 5: 3. On 1st April, 2023 the balance in their fixed capital accounts were ₹ 25,00,000 and ₹ 15,00,000 respectively. The profit of the firm for the year ended 31st March, 2024 was ₹ 24,00,000. Calculate their share of profit if:
(i) the partnership deed is silent as to the payment of interest on capital.
(ii) the partnership deed provides for interest on capital @ 10% per annum.

key_points: Case (i): When the deed is silent, no interest on capital is allowed. The entire profit of ₹ 24,00,000 is distributed in the 5:3 ratio.
Case (ii): When the deed provides for 10% interest on capital. Calculate IOC: Sonia = 25,00,000 * 10% = ₹ 2,50,000. Shruti = 15,00,000 * 10% = ₹ 1,50,000. Total IOC = ₹ 4,00,000.
Calculate divisible profit for Case (ii): 24,00,000 - 4,00,000 = ₹ 20,00,000.
Distribute divisible profit in 5:3 ratio: Sonia = 20,00,000 * 5/8 = ₹ 12,50,000. Shruti = 20,00,000 * 3/8 = ₹ 7,50,000.

sub_questions.solution:
In situation (i), where the partnership deed is silent regarding the payment of interest on capital, the rules of the Indian Partnership Act stipulate that no interest is to be provided. Consequently, the entire net profit of ₹ 24,00,000 is distributed to Sonia and Shruti in their profit-sharing ratio of 5:3. Sonia's share of the profit becomes 5/8 of ₹ 24,00,000, which equals ₹ 15,00,000, and Shruti's share is 3/8, amounting to ₹ 9,00,000.

In situation (ii), the deed specifies 10% per annum interest on capital. The interest calculated on Sonia's capital of ₹ 25,00,000 is ₹ 2,50,000, and on Shruti's capital of ₹ 15,00,000, it is ₹ 1,50,000. The total interest on capital amounts to ₹ 4,00,000. This interest is deducted from the net profit to arrive at the divisible profit, which is ₹ 24,00,000 - ₹ 4,00,000 = ₹ 20,00,000. This divisible profit is then shared in the 5:3 ratio. Sonia's share of the divisible profit is 5/8 of ₹ 20,00,000, which is ₹ 12,50,000. Shruti's share is 3/8, which comes to ₹ 7,50,000.

sub_questions.text_english: Mallark Ltd. purchased assets of book value ₹ 40,00,000 and took over liabilities of ₹ 5,00,000 from Naroha Ltd. It was agreed that the purchase consideration, ₹ 36,00,000 be paid by issuing 7% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a premium of 20%. Record the journal entries in the books of Mallark Ltd. for the above transactions.

key_points: Determine Net Assets acquired: Assets (40,00,000) - Liabilities (5,00,000) = 35,00,000.
Compare with Purchase Consideration (36,00,000). The excess 1,00,000 is treated as Goodwill.
Record acquisition: Debit Assets (40L), Debit Goodwill (1L), Credit Liabilities (5L), Credit Naroha Ltd (36L).
Calculate number of debentures: 36,00,000 / 120 (Issue price) = 30,000 debentures.
Record payment: Debit Naroha Ltd (36L), Credit 7% Debentures A/c (30L), Credit Securities Premium (6L).

sub_questions.solution:
Upon taking over a business, if the purchase consideration is higher than the net value of the assets taken over, the difference is debited to the Goodwill Account. The net assets value is the assets (₹ 40,00,000) less the liabilities (₹ 5,00,000), which equals ₹ 35,00,000. Since the agreed purchase consideration is ₹ 36,00,000, there is a Goodwill of ₹ 1,00,000. The acquisition journal entry will debit Sundry Assets by ₹ 40,00,000, debit Goodwill by ₹ 1,00,000, credit Sundry Liabilities by ₹ 5,00,000, and credit the vendor (Naroha Ltd.) by ₹ 36,00,000. 

Next, the purchase consideration is discharged by issuing 7% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a 20% premium, making the issue price ₹ 120 per debenture. To find the number of debentures issued, the total consideration of ₹ 36,00,000 is divided by ₹ 120, yielding 30,000 debentures. The payment journal entry will debit Naroha Ltd. by ₹ 36,00,000, credit 7% Debentures Account with the face value (30,000 * 100) equal to ₹ 30,00,000, and credit Securities Premium Account with the premium amount (30,000 * 20) equal to ₹ 6,00,000.

It paid the purchase consideration by issue of 46,000, 8% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a discount of 10%. Record the journal entries in the books of Sunlock Ltd.

key_points: Determine Net Assets acquired: Assets (50,00,000) - Liabilities (6,00,000) = 44,00,000.
Calculate Purchase Consideration: 46,000 debentures * 90 (Issue price) = 41,40,000.
Compare Net Assets with Purchase Consideration. Since Net Assets (44L) > Purchase Consideration (41.4L), the difference (2,60,000) is credited to Capital Reserve.
Record acquisition: Debit Assets (50L), Credit Liabilities (6L), Credit Moondock Ltd (41.4L), Credit Capital Reserve (2.6L).
Record payment: Debit Moondock Ltd (41.4L), Debit Discount on Issue of Debentures (4.6L), Credit 8% Debentures A/c (46L).

sub_questions.solution:
The purchase consideration must first be determined based on the debentures issued. Sunlock Ltd. issues 46,000 debentures at a 10% discount on a ₹ 100 face value. This makes the issue price ₹ 90. The total purchase consideration is therefore 46,000 * 90 = ₹ 41,40,000. 
When a business is taken over, the net asset value is calculated as the total assets taken over (₹ 50,00,000) minus the liabilities taken over (₹ 6,00,000), equating to ₹ 44,00,000. Because the net assets of ₹ 44,00,000 surpass the agreed purchase consideration of ₹ 41,40,000, the resulting capital profit of ₹ 2,60,000 is transferred to the Capital Reserve. 
The acquisition journal entry debits Sundry Assets with ₹ 50,00,000, credits Sundry Liabilities with ₹ 6,00,000, credits the vendor (Moondock Ltd.) with ₹ 41,40,000, and credits Capital Reserve with ₹ 2,60,000. 
For the settlement, the journal entry involves debiting Moondock Ltd. by ₹ 41,40,000, debiting Discount on Issue of Debentures with the total discount amount (46,000 * 10 = ₹ 4,60,000), and crediting 8% Debentures Account with the total face value (46,000 * 100 = ₹ 46,00,000).

PQ Ltd. invited applications for issuing 6,000, 11% debentures of ₹ 100 each at a premium of ₹ 10 per debenture. The amount was payable as follows:
On Application ₹ 30 per debenture
On Allotment ₹ 80 per debenture (including premium)
The debentures were fully subscribed and all money was duly received. Pass necessary journal entries for the above transactions in the books of PQ Ltd.

key_points: Bank A/c Dr. 1,80,000 to Debenture Application A/c 1,80,000 (For application money received on 6,000 debentures @ 30).
Debenture Application A/c Dr. 1,80,000 to 11% Debentures A/c 1,80,000 (For transferring application money to Debentures A/c).
Debenture Allotment A/c Dr. 4,80,000 to 11% Debentures A/c 4,20,000, to Securities Premium A/c 60,000 (For allotment money due on 6,000 debentures @ 80 each including 10 premium).
Bank A/c Dr. 4,80,000 to Debenture Allotment A/c 4,80,000 (For allotment money received).

questions.solution:
The issue involves 6,000 debentures with a face value of ₹ 100 each, issued at a premium of ₹ 10 per debenture, making the total issue price ₹ 110. The payment schedule requires ₹ 30 on application and ₹ 80 on allotment. The ₹ 80 allotment money is inclusive of the ₹ 10 premium, meaning ₹ 70 corresponds to the debenture capital. 
First, upon receiving the application money, the Bank Account is debited, and the Debenture Application Account is credited by 6,000 * 30 = ₹ 1,80,000. 
This application money is subsequently transferred to the 11% Debentures Account. Thus, the Debenture Application Account is debited, and the 11% Debentures Account is credited by ₹ 1,80,000. 
When the allotment becomes due, the Debenture Allotment Account is debited with the full amount expected, which is 6,000 * 80 = ₹ 4,80,000. In correspondence, the 11% Debentures Account is credited with the principal portion (6,000 * 70 = ₹ 4,20,000) and the Securities Premium Account is credited with the premium portion (6,000 * 10 = ₹ 60,000). 
Finally, when the allotment money is received, the Bank Account is debited, and the Debenture Allotment Account is credited by the received sum of ₹ 4,80,000.

questions.text_english: Gopal, Heera and Iqbal were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses equally. Iqbal died on 1st April, 2022. Final dues payable to Iqbal's executor as on the date of death amounted to ₹ 4,00,000. Starting from 31st March, 2023, the executor was to be paid in two equal annual instalments of ₹ 2,00,000 each, with interest @ 10% per annum. Accounts are closed on 31st March every year. Prepare Iqbal's executor's account till he is finally paid.

key_points: Record opening balance on 1st April 2022: By Iqbal's Capital A/c ₹ 4,00,000.
Calculate interest for Year 1 (31st March 2023) on ₹ 4,00,000 @ 10% = ₹ 40,000. Credit to Executor's A/c.
Record first instalment payment on 31st March 2023: To Bank A/c ₹ 2,40,000 (Principal ₹ 2,00,000 + Interest ₹ 40,000).
Calculate and carry down closing balance on 31st March 2023: To Balance c/d ₹ 2,00,000.
Bring down opening balance on 1st April 2023: By Balance b/d ₹ 2,00,000.
Calculate interest for Year 2 (31st March 2024) on ₹ 2,00,000 @ 10% = ₹ 20,000. Credit to Executor's A/c.
Record second instalment payment on 31st March 2024: To Bank A/c ₹ 2,20,000 (Principal ₹ 2,00,000 + Interest ₹ 20,000). Account is now settled.

questions.solution:
The preparation of Iqbal's Executor's Account begins on the date of his death, 1st April 2022. The initial amount due, which is transferred from Iqbal's Capital Account, is credited to the Executor's Account as ₹ 4,00,000. 
At the end of the first financial year on 31st March 2023, interest is calculated on the outstanding balance of ₹ 4,00,000 at a rate of 10% per annum. This amounts to ₹ 40,000, which is credited to the account. On the same date, the first installment is paid. The payment consists of the principal portion of ₹ 2,00,000 plus the accrued interest of ₹ 40,000, making the total payment ₹ 2,40,000, which is debited to the account (To Bank). The remaining balance to be carried forward to the next year is ₹ 2,00,000. 
On 1st April 2023, this balance is brought down on the credit side. By the end of the second financial year on 31st March 2024, interest is computed on the new outstanding balance of ₹ 2,00,000 at 10%, which equals ₹ 20,000. This is credited to the account. The second and final installment is then paid, comprising the remaining principal of ₹ 2,00,000 plus the new interest of ₹ 20,000. Thus, ₹ 2,20,000 is debited to the account (To Bank), bringing the Executor's Account balance to nil, marking the full settlement of the dues.

questions.text_english:
Manav and Namit were partners in a firm sharing profits and losses in the ratio of 3: 2. Their Balance Sheet as at 31st March, 2024 was as follows:
Balance Sheet of Manav and Namit as at 31st March, 2024
[Table in Image]
The firm was dissolved on the above date and the following transactions took place:
(i) Stock was given to creditors in full settlement of their account.
(ii) Investments were taken over by Manav at 120% of book value.
(iii) Bad debts amounted to ₹ 2,00,000.
(iv) Machinery was realised at 50% discount.
(v) Realisation expenses amounted to ₹ 1,00,000 which were paid by Namit.
Prepare Realisation Account.

key_points: Transfer assets to Realisation A/c debit side: Machinery 8,00,000; Investments 5,00,000; Debtors 12,00,000; Stock 3,00,000. Total = 28,00,000.
Transfer external liabilities to Realisation A/c credit side: Bank Overdraft 9,00,000; Creditors 10,00,000. Total = 19,00,000.
(i) Creditors took over stock in full settlement: No journal entry is required for the stock or the creditors.
(ii) Investments taken over by Manav @ 120%: Book value 5,00,000 * 120% = 6,00,000. Credit Realisation A/c by 6,00,000 (By Manav's Capital A/c).
(iii) Debtors realization: Total Debtors 12,00,000. Bad debts 2,00,000. Realized = 10,00,000. Credit Realisation A/c by 10,00,000 (By Cash/Bank A/c).
(iv) Machinery realized @ 50% discount: Book value 8,00,000 * 50% = 4,00,000. Credit Realisation A/c by 4,00,000 (By Cash/Bank A/c).
(v) Realisation expenses paid by Namit: Debit Realisation A/c by 1,00,000 (To Namit's Capital A/c).

Bank Overdraft payment: Since there is no information about Bank Overdraft settlement, it must be paid in full (assuming it was transferred to Realisation). Debit Realisation A/c by 9,00,000 (To Cash/Bank A/c).

Calculate final profit/loss: Total Debit = 28,00,000 (assets) + 1,00,000 (exp) + 9,00,000 (Bank OD) = 38,00,000. Total Credit = 19,00,000 (liab) + 6,00,000 (Manav) + 14,00,000 (Bank) = 39,00,000. Net Profit = 1,00,000.
Distribute Profit to partners in 3:2: Manav's share = 60,000; Namit's share = 40,000. Debit Realisation A/c by 1,00,000 (To Profit transferred to Capital accounts).

questions.solution:
The Realisation Account is prepared by first transferring all asset and liability accounts (excluding cash/bank and partner's capital). Assets totaling ₹ 28,00,000 (Machinery ₹ 8L, Investments ₹ 5L, Debtors ₹ 12L, Stock ₹ 3L) are transferred to the debit side. Liabilities totaling ₹ 19,00,000 (Bank Overdraft ₹ 9L, Creditors ₹ 10L) are transferred to the credit side.
For the asset realizations and liability settlements:
(i) Stock given to creditors in full settlement requires no entry as the liability and asset cancel each other out completely.
(ii) Investments taken over by Manav at 120% of book value (₹ 5L * 120%) are recorded on the credit side as 'By Manav's Capital A/c' for ₹ 6,00,000.
(iii) Debtors had ₹ 2,00,000 as bad debts, so ₹ 10,00,000 (12L - 2L) is realised. This is credited as 'By Cash A/c'.
(iv) Machinery realised at a 50% discount yields ₹ 4,00,000. This is also credited under 'By Cash A/c'. Total Cash Realised = ₹ 14,00,000.
(v) Realisation expenses paid by Namit are recorded on the debit side as 'To Namit's Capital A/c' for ₹ 1,00,000.
Additionally, since no instruction was given regarding the settlement of Bank Overdraft, it must be paid off in full. Thus, ₹ 9,00,000 is debited as 'To Cash A/c'.
Comparing the debit and credit totals reveals a credit excess of ₹ 1,00,000, which represents the profit on realisation. This profit is distributed to the partners in their profit-sharing ratio of 3:2. The debit side will record 'To Profit transferred to Partners' Capital A/cs' with Manav receiving ₹ 60,000 and Namit receiving ₹ 40,000. Both sides of the Realisation Account will balance at ₹ 39,00,000.

key_points: Record application money received: 3,00,000 shares * 20 = 60,00,000.

Allocate Application & Allotment money: Share Capital = 2,00,000 * 3 = 6,00,000. Securities Premium = 2,00,000 * 17 = 34,00,000. Transfer excess to Calls-in-Advance = 1,00,000 shares * 20 = 20,00,000.
Make First & Final Call due: Share First & Final Call Dr. 20,00,000. To Share Capital = 2,00,000 * 7 = 14,00,000. To Securities Premium = 2,00,000 * 3 = 6,00,000.
Determine Deepali's allotted shares: She applied for 2,000 shares in Cat (i). Allotted ratio is 1,50,000 / 2,00,000. Thus, allotted = 2,000 * (15/20) = 1,500 shares.
Calculate Deepali's excess application money: Excess shares = 500. Excess money = 500 * 20 = 10,000.
Calculate Deepali's call money due: 1,500 * 10 = 15,000. Net amount not paid (Calls-in-Arrears) = 15,000 - 10,000 (advance) = 5,000.

Record call money received: Total due 20,00,000. Total advance transferred to call 20,00,000. Wait, if total advance is 20L and call due is 20L, then no money is received on call? Let's check: Cat I excess = 50,000 * 20 = 10L. Call due = 1.5L * 10 = 15L. So Cat I pays 5L. Cat II excess = 50,000 * 20 = 10L. Call due = 50k * 10 = 5L. So Cat II has 5L extra which must be refunded! The question says "adjusted towards sums due on first and final call". It doesn't explicitly say refund, but standard practice requires refunding the unadjustable excess. Thus, Calls in advance is 15,00,000 and Bank (refund) is 5,00,000.
Re-evaluate allocation: App recd = 60L. Cap = 6L. SPR = 34L. Call Adv = 15L. Bank (Refund) = 5L.
Re-evaluate Call Receipt: Due = 20L. Less Adv = 15L. Net expected = 5L (all from Cat I). Deepali (Cat I) arrears = 15,000 - 10,000 (her advance) = 5,000. Bank receives = 5,00,000 - 5,000 = 4,95,000.

Record forfeiture: Share Capital Dr (1500 * 10 = 15,000). SPR Dr (1500 * 3 = 4,500, since premium on call not paid). To Share Forfeiture (Amount paid = 40,000 applied for * 20 = 40,000 total paid. Less SPR on allotted shares 1500 * 17 = 25,500. So forfeiture is 40,000 - 25,500 = 14,500). To Calls-in-Arrears 5,000.

Balance Sheet of Chandan, Deepak and Elvish as at 31st March, 2024
[Balance Sheet Table in Image]
Chandan retired from the firm on 1st April, 2024 on the following terms:
(i) Fixed assets were to be depreciated by 10%.
(ii) Debtors of ₹ 30,000 were to be written off as bad debts.
(iii) Goodwill of the firm was valued at ₹ 6,00,000 and the retiring partner's share is adjusted through the capital accounts of the remaining partners.
(iv) Chandan was paid through cash brought in by Deepak and Elvish in such a way so as to make their capitals proportionate to their new profit sharing ratio.
Prepare Revaluation Account and Partners' Capital Accounts.

key_points: Revaluation Account: Debit side = Fixed Assets (1,50,000) and Bad Debts (30,000). Total Loss = 1,80,000. Distribute to Chandan (36,000), Deepak (72,000), and Elvish (72,000).
Goodwill adjustment: Chandan's share is 1/5 of 6,00,000 = 1,20,000. Gaining ratio is 2:2 (or 1:1). Deepak and Elvish are debited by 60,000 each. Chandan is credited by 1,20,000.
General Reserve distribution (4,50,000): Chandan gets 90,000, Deepak gets 1,80,000, Elvish gets 1,80,000.
Chandan's Settlement: Adjusted Capital = 7,00,000 + 90,000 + 1,20,000 - 36,000 = ₹ 8,74,000. This is paid in cash.

Determine New Capitals: Total Capital of new firm = Combined adjusted capitals of Deepak and Elvish + Amount paid to Chandan. Deepak's adjusted cap = 5L + 1.8L - 72k - 60k = 5,48,000. Elvish's adjusted cap = 3L + 1.8L - 72k - 60k = 3,48,000. Total = 5,48,000 + 3,48,000 + 8,74,000 = ₹ 17,70,000.
New Capital setup: New ratio is 1:1. Each partner's new capital = 17,70,000 / 2 = ₹ 8,85,000.
Cash adjustments: Deepak brings in 8,85,000 - 5,48,000 = ₹ 3,37,000. Elvish brings in 8,85,000 - 3,48,000 = ₹ 5,37,000.

questions.text_english: The Quick Ratio of a company is 2: 1. Which of the following transactions will result in decrease of this ratio?

options_english.C: Sale of goods at a profit

questions.solution:
Quick Ratio is the ratio of Quick Assets to Current Liabilities. Let Quick Assets be 200 and Current Liabilities be 100. 
- (A) Payment of outstanding salary: Both Quick Assets (cash) and Current Liabilities decrease by the same amount. E.g., 200-20 / 100-20 = 180/80 = 2.25. The ratio increases.
- (B) Cash received from debtors: One quick asset (cash) increases, another (debtors) decreases. No net change in Quick Assets. The ratio remains unchanged.
- (C) Sale of goods at a profit: Debtors/Cash (quick assets) increase, while Stock (not a quick asset) decreases. Total Quick Assets increase. The ratio increases.
- (D) Purchase of goods for cash: Cash (a quick asset) decreases while Stock (not a quick asset) increases. Thus, total Quick Assets decrease while Current Liabilities remain unchanged. The Quick Ratio will decrease.
Therefore, option D is the correct answer.

key_points: Identify Profit After Tax: ₹ 6,30,000 and Tax Rate: 30%.

sub_questions.solution:
To find the Interest Coverage Ratio, we first need to determine the Earnings Before Interest and Tax (EBIT). The problem provides the Profit After Tax (PAT) as ₹ 6,30,000 with a tax rate of 30%. This means the PAT represents 70% of the Profit Before Tax (PBT). 
Profit Before Tax (PBT) = PAT / 0.70 = ₹ 6,30,000 / 0.70 = ₹ 9,00,000.
Next, we calculate the long-term interest expense. The firm holds 15% Debentures valued at ₹ 20,00,000. 
Interest on Debentures = 15% of ₹ 20,00,000 = ₹ 3,00,000.
We then add the interest back to the PBT to find EBIT. 
EBIT = PBT + Interest = ₹ 9,00,000 + ₹ 3,00,000 = ₹ 12,00,000.
Finally, the Interest Coverage Ratio is calculated by dividing EBIT by the Interest expense: 
Interest Coverage Ratio = ₹ 12,00,000 / ₹ 3,00,000 = 4 times.

key_points: Calculate Total Sales (Revenue from Operations): Since Gross Profit is 20% on sales, Cost is 80% on sales. Total Sales = 8,00,000 / 80% = ₹ 10,00,000.
Establish relationship between Cash and Credit Sales: Let Credit Sales = x. Cash Sales = x/4. Total Sales = x + x/4 = 5x/4.
Calculate Credit Sales: 5x/4 = 10,00,000. Credit Sales (x) = ₹ 8,00,000.
Calculate Average Trade Receivables: Credit Sales / TR Turnover Ratio = 8,00,000 / 5 = ₹ 1,60,000.
Set up equation for Opening and Closing TR: Let Opening = y. Closing = y + 40,000. Average = (y + y + 40,000) / 2 = y + 20,000.
Solve for y: y + 20,000 = 1,60,000. Opening TR (y) = ₹ 1,40,000. Closing TR = ₹ 1,80,000.

sub_questions.solution:
Working Notes:
The Gross Profit Ratio is 20% on total sales (Revenue from Operations). Therefore, the Cost of Revenue from Operations represents the remaining 80% of sales.
Total Sales = Cost of Revenue / 80% = ₹ 8,00,000 / 0.80 = ₹ 10,00,000.

We are given that Total Sales = Cash Sales + Credit Sales.
Let Credit Sales be x. The problem states Cash Sales are 1/4th of Credit Sales, so Cash Sales = x/4.
x + x/4 = ₹ 10,00,000
(5/4)x = ₹ 10,00,000
x (Credit Sales) = ₹ 10,00,000 × 4/5 = ₹ 8,00,000.

The Trade Receivables Turnover Ratio is calculated as Net Credit Sales divided by Average Trade Receivables. 
Average Trade Receivables = ₹ 8,00,000 / 5 = ₹ 1,60,000.

Let Opening Trade Receivables be y. 
Closing Trade Receivables are ₹ 40,000 more, so they are y + 40,000.
The formula for average is (Opening + Closing) / 2.
₹ 1,60,000 = (y + y + 40,000) / 2
₹ 1,60,000 = y + 20,000
y (Opening Trade Receivables) = ₹ 1,40,000.
Closing Trade Receivables = ₹ 1,40,000 + ₹ 40,000 = ₹ 1,80,000.

Thus, Opening Trade Receivables are ₹ 1,40,000 and Closing Trade Receivables are ₹ 1,80,000.

questions.solution:
To calculate the Cash Flows from Investing Activities, we systematically analyze the changes in non-current asset balances alongside the additional information provided.

1. Plant and Machinery: Since accumulated depreciation is not given separately, we prepare the Plant and Machinery Account on a Written Down Value (WDV) basis. 
Opening Balance = ₹ 6,00,000. 
The WDV of the machine sold is its cost minus its specific depreciation: ₹ 60,000 - ₹ 18,000 = ₹ 42,000. 
The machine was sold for ₹ 48,000, creating an inflow of ₹ 48,000. 
The current year's depreciation charged is ₹ 60,000. 
Closing Balance is ₹ 8,00,000.

2. 10% Long Term Investments: The balance decreased from ₹ 4,50,000 to ₹ 2,50,000, indicating a sale. Cash Inflow from sale = ₹ 2,00,000.

3. Investment in shares of Pinnacle Ltd.: The balance increased from ₹ 5,00,000 to ₹ 14,00,000, indicating a purchase. Cash Outflow for purchase = ₹ 9,00,000.

4. Patents: The balance decreased from ₹ 1,50,000 to Nil. As stated, they were sold at their book value. Cash Inflow from sale = ₹ 1,50,000.

6. Income received on investments:

Interest received on Long Term Investments = ₹ 45,000 (Inflow).

Outflows: Purchase of Machinery (3,02,000) + Purchase of Pinnacle Shares (9,00,000) + Purchase of Goodwill (40,000) = ₹ 12,42,000.
Net Cash Used in Investing Activities = 4,83,000 - 12,42,000 = (₹ 7,59,000).

questions.text_english: Differentiate between tailored and specific softwares on any three basis.

key_points: Nature/Target Audience: Tailored software is custom-built exclusively for the unique needs of a single specific user or organization. Specific (Ready-to-use/Off-the-shelf) software is mass-produced for a general audience with common needs.
Cost: Tailored software is generally highly expensive due to dedicated development time. Specific software is relatively cheaper as development costs are distributed among many buyers.
Implementation Time: Tailored software takes a long time to develop, test, and implement. Specific software is available for immediate installation and use.
Flexibility/Adaptability: Tailored software is highly flexible and can be modified precisely as the business changes. Specific software offers low flexibility and only allows limited customization.

questions.solution:
The differences between Tailored Software (custom-built) and Specific/Ready-to-use Software can be outlined on the following three bases:

1. Target Audience and Nature: 
Tailored software is specifically designed and developed from scratch to meet the exact, unique requirements of a single, specific organization. In contrast, Specific (or off-the-shelf) software is mass-produced by software companies to cater to the generalized, common needs of a large number of users across an industry.

2. Cost of Acquisition: 
Tailored software is significantly more expensive because the entire cost of development, programming, and testing is borne by the single purchasing company. Specific software is relatively much cheaper because the development costs are distributed across thousands of retail buyers.

3. Time Required for Implementation: 
Tailored software requires a prolonged period before it can be used, as it undergoes lengthy phases of requirement analysis, coding, and debugging. Specific software, being pre-packaged, is available immediately and can be installed and utilized right away.

sub_questions.text_english: What are the different phases of accounting cycle which can be processed through the use of computers?

key_points: Data Entry/Recording: The initial input of daily transactions using electronic vouchers.
Journalizing: Automatic chronological recording of transactions into the digital journal.
Ledger Posting: Automatic and immediate classification and posting of journal entries into respective ledger accounts.
Trial Balance Preparation: Automatic generation of a Trial Balance to verify the arithmetical accuracy of the ledgers.
Financial Statement Generation: The automated compilation of the Trading and Profit & Loss Account and the Balance Sheet at the end of the period.

sub_questions.solution:
The accounting cycle consists of a logical sequence of steps to process financial information. With the use of computers, nearly all phases are automated after the initial data entry. The key phases processed through computers are:

1. Recording of Transactions (Data Entry): This is the only manual phase where an operator inputs raw transaction data (like sales, purchases, payments) into the software using customized digital voucher screens.
2. Journalizing: The software automatically processes the entered data and chronologically records the transactions in the system's digital journal.
3. Ledger Posting: Unlike manual accounting, the computer immediately and automatically posts the journal entries to their respective individual ledger accounts, updating their balances in real-time.
4. Preparation of Trial Balance: At any given moment, the software can extract the balances of all ledger accounts and automatically generate a mathematically accurate Trial Balance.
5. Preparation of Final Accounts: At the end of the accounting period, the software utilizes the Trial Balance data to automatically generate the final financial statements, namely the Statement of Profit and Loss and the Balance Sheet.

questions.text_english: Which error appears when there is formula or function with 'invalid' numeric value? How can you correct it?

key_points: The error that appears is the #NUM! error.
It occurs when a formula or function contains invalid numeric values.
Correction 1: Check the formula arguments to ensure they are within the acceptable mathematical limits (e.g., preventing calculating the square root of a negative number).
Correction 2: Ensure the function isn't iterating to a result that is too large or too small for Excel to display.
Correction 3: Check iterative functions like IRR or RATE to ensure they are converging. You may need to provide a different guess value.

questions.solution:
When a formula or function in Excel contains an 'invalid' numeric value, the `#NUM!` error is displayed. This error typically signifies that the mathematical operation being attempted is impossible or out of bounds for Excel to process (e.g., trying to find the square root of a negative number, or a number being too large or too small to be represented).

To correct the `#NUM!` error, you can follow these steps:
1. Check Mathematical Logic: Review the formula to ensure you are not performing impossible mathematical operations. For example, ensure that an `SQRT` function is not referencing a negative number. If dealing with negative numbers, use the `ABS` function to convert them to positive if appropriate.
2. Verify Value Limits: Ensure that the values being entered or calculated do not exceed Excel's limits. Excel cannot handle numbers greater than $10^{308}$ or smaller than $10^{-308}$. 
3. Check Iterative Functions: If using financial functions that rely on iteration (like `IRR` or `RATE`) and Excel cannot find a result after multiple attempts, it will throw a `#NUM!` error. You can correct this by providing a better 'guess' argument to help the function converge on the correct answer.
